Thomas M. Hoenig, the President of the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City, dissented from the December 2010 FOMC decision to hold the target range for the federal funds rate at 0 to 1/4 percent. He believed that economic conditions were improving and that the current accommodative monetary policy was inconsistent with the Committee's long-run mandate. Hoenig argued that maintaining such a stance would increase the risk of future imbalances and could lead to higher inflation expectations over time. He advocated for preparing markets for a reduction in policy accommodation, but the Committee decided to maintain the status quo. [2010-12-14/policyAction/1, 2010-12-14/policyAction/11]

Although she was fully supportive of the actions taken to promote market stability and credit flow, Mester preferred a reduction to 1/2 to 3/4 percent at this meeting [2020-03-15/policyAction/17].

Michelle W. Bowman dissented from the September 2024 meeting's decision to lower the target range for the federal funds rate to 4-3/4 to 5 percent.
